Production checklist

  • Secrets: never in code; use env vars or Secrets Manager. Rotate on exposure.
  • Authentication: protect endpoints; rate limit per user, not just IP.
  • Observability: structured logs, metrics (latency, errors, tokens, cost), traces.
  • Cost controls: per-user daily caps, alert on budget burn.
  • Rate limiting: 429s with Retry-After; protect upstream model.
  • Graceful degradation: cache, fallback to smaller model, queue overflow.
  • Versioning: pin model versions and prompt versions; test before rollout.
  • Privacy: minimize data sent to the LLM; redact PII; document retention policy.
  • Safety: content moderation on inputs and outputs; abuse detection.
  • Health/readiness checks: /health, /ready; orchestrator-friendly.
⚠ COMMON PITFALL

The single biggest production failure mode is uncapped spend. A bug in iteration logic, a malicious user, or an autoscaling event can burn $5,000 overnight. ALWAYS: per-user daily caps, total daily caps, billing alerts at the provider, monitoring on token rate. Treat LLM cost like database connections — finite, monitored, alarmed.

import time, hashlib, json, collections, threading, random

print("1. Cache what repeats. Measure the hit rate before you tune anything else.")
class Cache:
    def __init__(self, maxsize=128):
        self.store = collections.OrderedDict(); self.maxsize = maxsize
        self.hits = self.misses = 0
    def key(self, model, messages, temperature):
        raw = json.dumps({"m": model, "msgs": messages, "t": temperature}, sort_keys=True)
        return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
    def get(self, k):
        if k in self.store:
            self.hits += 1; self.store.move_to_end(k); return self.store[k]
        self.misses += 1; return None
    def put(self, k, v):
        self.store[k] = v; self.store.move_to_end(k)
        if len(self.store) > self.maxsize: self.store.popitem(last=False)
    @property
    def hit_rate(self):
        t = self.hits + self.misses
        return self.hits / t if t else 0.0

cache = Cache()
def call_model(model, messages, temperature=0.0, cache_on=True):
    """LABELLED STUB for the API call: sleeps to imitate latency. No network."""
    k = cache.key(model, messages, temperature)
    if cache_on and temperature == 0:
        hit = cache.get(k)
        if hit is not None: return hit, True
    time.sleep(0.02)
    out = f"[stub answer for {messages[-1]['content'][:24]!r}]"
    if cache_on and temperature == 0: cache.put(k, out)
    return out, False

questions = ["What is a p-value?", "What is a p-value?", "Explain RAG.",
             "What is a p-value?", "Explain RAG.", "What is overfitting?"] * 4
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for q in questions:
    call_model("m1", [{"role": "user", "content": q}])
cached_time = time.perf_counter() - t0
cache2 = cache; cache = Cache()
t0 = time.perf_counter()
for q in questions:
    call_model("m1", [{"role": "user", "content": q}], cache_on=False)
uncached_time = time.perf_counter() - t0
print(f"   {len(questions)} requests, {len(set(questions))} distinct")
print(f"   without cache {uncached_time:.3f}s")
print(f"   with cache    {cached_time:.3f}s   ({uncached_time/cached_time:.1f}x faster)")
print(f"   hit rate {cache2.hit_rate:.1%} ({cache2.hits} hits, {cache2.misses} misses)")
print("   Only cache at temperature 0. Caching a random sample means every user gets")
print("   the first user's roll of the dice.")

print("\n2. Rate limit yourself, before the provider does it for you.")
class TokenBucket:
    def __init__(self, rate, burst):
        self.rate, self.capacity = rate, burst
        self.tokens = burst; self.last = time.perf_counter(); self.lock = threading.Lock()
    def take(self, n=1):
        with self.lock:
            now = time.perf_counter()
            self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now - self.last) * self.rate)
            self.last = now
            if self.tokens >= n:
                self.tokens -= n; return True
            return False
bucket = TokenBucket(rate=20, burst=5)
allowed = blocked = 0
for _ in range(20):
    if bucket.take(): allowed += 1
    else: blocked += 1
    time.sleep(0.005)
print(f"   20 rapid requests against 20/s with a burst of 5 -> {allowed} allowed, {blocked} throttled")
print("   A token bucket allows a short burst and then holds you to the average, which")
print("   is exactly the shape most provider limits take.")

print("\n3. Log every call, with the fields you will actually need at 2am.")
LOG = []
def logged_call(user, model, messages, **kw):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    err = None
    try:
        out, was_cached = call_model(model, messages, **kw)
    except Exception as e:
        out, was_cached, err = None, False, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
    dur = time.perf_counter() - t0
    in_tok = sum(len(m["content"]) for m in messages) // 4
    out_tok = len(out) // 4 if out else 0
    LOG.append({"ts": len(LOG), "user": user, "model": model,
                "prompt_sha": cache.key(model, messages, 0)[:8],
                "in_tokens": in_tok, "out_tokens": out_tok,
                "latency_ms": round(dur * 1000, 1), "cached": was_cached,
                "error": err, "cost_usd": round(in_tok*3e-6 + out_tok*15e-6, 6)})
    return out
for i, q in enumerate(["What is a p-value?", "Explain RAG.", "What is a p-value?"]):
    logged_call(f"user{i%2}", "m1", [{"role": "user", "content": q}])
for row in LOG:
    print(f"   {json.dumps(row)}")
print("   The prompt hash, not the prompt: you can group identical requests without")
print("   storing whatever the user typed into your logs.")

print("\n4. Aggregate the log - that is your dashboard.")
total_cost = sum(r["cost_usd"] for r in LOG)
lat = sorted(r["latency_ms"] for r in LOG)
def pct(p): return lat[min(len(lat)-1, int(len(lat)*p/100))]
print(f"   calls {len(LOG)}   errors {sum(1 for r in LOG if r['error'])}"
      f"   cached {sum(1 for r in LOG if r['cached'])}")
print(f"   latency p50 {pct(50):.1f} ms   p95 {pct(95):.1f} ms   max {lat[-1]:.1f} ms")
print(f"   cost this sample ${total_cost:.6f}; at 50,000 calls/month "
      f"${total_cost/len(LOG)*50_000:,.2f}")
print("   Track the p95, not the mean. The mean hides the tail, and the tail is what")
print("   users complain about.")

print("\n5. Fail softly. Decide the fallback before you need it.")
def with_fallback(primary, fallback, cached_answer=None):
    for name, fn in [("primary", primary), ("fallback", fallback)]:
        try:
            return name, fn()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"      {name} failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    if cached_answer: return "stale cache", cached_answer
    return "degraded", "Sorry - that service is unavailable right now."
def broken(): raise TimeoutError("primary model timed out")
def cheaper(): return "[stub answer from the smaller model]"
print(f"   {with_fallback(broken, cheaper)}")
stale = "[yesterday's cached answer]"
print(f"   {with_fallback(broken, broken, cached_answer=stale)}")
print(f"   {with_fallback(broken, broken)}")
print("   A degraded answer beats a stack trace. Decide the order: retry, cheaper model,")
print("   stale cache, honest apology.")

print("\n6. The production checklist.")
for item, why in [("timeout on every call", "the default is no timeout at all"),
                  ("retry with exponential backoff", "on 429 and 5xx only, never on 400"),
                  ("cache at temperature 0", "the cheapest request is the one you skip"),

🧠 The Aistote Method (J-Method)

THE IDEA
The Aistote app is built on two of the most evidence-backed study techniques — active recall and spaced repetition — run in short, intense 25-minute blocks (its "J-Method"). Instead of slowly re-reading, you spend the time testing yourself and re-testing what you miss. This app already has every tool the method needs.
THE 3-STEP LOOP
StepWhat you doWhere in this app
1. ConvertTurn the material into questions instead of re-reading it.Open a section, skim the lesson once, then jump to its Quiz.
2. RecallAnswer from memory first — no peeking — then check.Take the section Quiz, or a PA / OA simulation; rate your confidence.
3. Space itRe-test only what you missed, on a growing schedule.Every miss becomes a Flashcard; review them on the app's spaced-repetition schedule.
A 25-MINUTE J-METHOD SESSION
TimeDo this
0–3 minSkim the lesson's key terms and the big idea — don't memorize yet, just get the lay of the land.
3–18 minTake the section quiz (or a 15-question drill). Try to recall the answer first, reveal it after.
18–23 minRedo only the questions you got wrong.
23–25 minSend the stubborn ones to Flashcards and note tomorrow's quick review.
Start the block with the ⚡ Focus timer (25 min) on any lesson — that is your J-Method session.
⚠️ THE ONE RULE
Always try to answer from memory before you look. The effort of retrieving is what actually builds the memory — re-reading feels productive but barely moves it.
WHY IT WORKS
Active recall (testing yourself) forces your brain to reconstruct the answer, which strengthens it far more than recognition. Spaced repetition reviews each fact just as you're about to forget it, moving it into long-term memory with the fewest reps. The 25-minute block simply makes you actually do both, every day.
DAILY RHYTHM
Two or three 25-minute J-Method blocks a day (new material in one, missed-question review in the next) beats a single long cram session — and it's how the Aistote method delivers "learn it in 25 minutes" instead of hours.

Comparison — Best for comparing a quantity across DISCRETE categories. Default to horizontal bars when category labels are long (they don't overlap).

Distribution — For visualizing the distribution of ONE numeric variable. Choose bin count carefully — too few hides structure, too many is noisy.

Relationship — The default for showing relationship between two numeric variables.

Change over time — The standard for time series. Time on x-axis, value on y-axis, connecting line shows the trajectory.

Geographic — Coloring regions by value. Good for showing how a metric varies across states/counties/countries.
